`POST /api/external/chat/stream` sends a message to your pod's AI and streams the answer back as Server-Sent Events.
The pod forwards the conversation to its **Intelligence Service** and records every turn. It needs an Intelligence
Service configured on the pod: on Synap Cloud it is; on a self-hosted pod see
[Self-hosted pod or Synap Cloud](/docs/use/cloud-vs-self-hosted#what-you-take-on-when-you-self-host).

To connect your own agent to your pod instead, use [MCP](/docs/build/agents/mcp).

## Before you start

Create an [API key](/docs/build/api-keys) with the `chat.stream` scope.

## List the channels you can chat in

```bash
curl https://pod.example.com/api/external/chat/channels \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SYNAP_API_KEY"
```

## Send a message

```bash
curl -N -X POST https://pod.example.com/api/external/chat/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SYNAP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "query": "What did I decide about the launch date?" }'
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | yes | Your message. |
| `channelId` | no | A channel from `/channels`. Without it, your personal AI channel is used. |
| `workspaceId` | no | The workspace to work in. |
| `agentType` | no | Which agent should answer. |
| `requestId` | no | A UUID you choose, to make a retry idempotent. Also accepted as the `X-Request-Id` header. |

## The response

The response is `text/event-stream`. Every turn is recorded on the pod:

- The `X-Synap-Turn-Id` response header carries the turn's ID.
- The first frame is always the turn frame:

  ```
  data: {"type":"turn","turnId":"…","requestId":"…"}
  ```

- The frames after it are the Intelligence Service's own stream, passed through unchanged. Their format is not
  documented here yet.

If the Intelligence Service cannot be reached or fails, the endpoint answers `502` with a JSON body
`{ "error": "…", "turnId": "…" }` instead of a stream. Service URLs and keys are never included in a response.

## Approving what the AI proposes

When the AI wants to change your data, the change becomes a **proposal**. A person approves it, for example in Relay
or the Browser app, or through the Hub REST API:

```bash
curl -X POST https://pod.example.com/api/hub/proposals/<proposalId>/approve \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SYNAP_API_KEY"
```

This needs a key with `hub-protocol.write` that belongs to a person. An agent's key is always refused here:
approving is a human step. `POST /api/hub/proposals/<proposalId>/reject` rejects a proposal, and
`GET /api/hub/proposals` lists them.
